comparisons.interpretation: Descriptive whole-case comparisons only, kept separate by window. No acceptance gate, pooled inference, or CPU/wall subtraction.

limitations: The diagnostic cycle-wall mode did not reproduce the original formal single-method p95 disadvantage in either window. This diagnostic does not withdraw the original formal tail findings.
Tail directions differ between modes and windows. Two opposite-order windows do not establish that clock instrumentation alone caused the reversal.
Both ADD and REMOVE contribute to selected cycle tails; these observations do not identify either phase as the root cause.
CPU intervals include instrumentation and may overlap across processes. No wall-minus-CPU or scheduler-wait inference is made.
Middle CPU sampling delays REMOVE; mode comparisons are observer calibration, never corrections subtracted from requests.
Each tail is selected by its own cycle p95 with all ties; per-operation samples are not independent experimental repeats. Windows are kept separate.
Affinity, thread count and process identity checks are boundary observations; last_processor is not a migration count.
REMOVE lifecycle may be investigated as a follow-up question; no additional optimization potential or performance gain is established.
Absolute paths, PIDs, process start times, monotonic measurement timestamps and device identity values are omitted. File labels and SHA-256 identities retain evidence linkage.
